observations: A head fills most of the frame, turned slightly, with thick black outlines defining rectangular glasses, a small hoop earring, and a garment with collar details against a flat olive-green background.
The hair is built from a dense tangle of black scribbled lines threaded with bright cyan, pink, and orange zigzag strokes that spike outward past the head's silhouette.
The face is filled with overlapping translucent blobs of pink, green, yellow, and muted purple, while a single bright red-orange lip shape anchors the lower right of the head.
reading: The flat olive field pushes the figure forward, giving the tangled neon-threaded hair a crackling presence against the stillness. Soft, cloudy color patches beneath the skin lines read as warmth seen through frosted glass—something held back. The dark rectangular glasses block the eyes entirely, creating a sealed-off quality. That single vivid lip becomes the only point of open expression, lending the composition a feeling of guarded cool.
contextAngle: In the owned rawblocks subset, this work sits between "nnxyz rawblocks #13" and "nnxyz rawblocks #15." All three feature head-and-shoulder compositions with black contour lines over layered color, but this piece uses a single flat background tone where its neighbors fill the field with pattern.

connections.reason: Both build a head from black contour lines over translucent color patches, but #13 marks the eyes with dark crosses on a warm gold ground while #14 hides them behind opaque glasses on cool olive.
Both show hair as a mass of looping black lines, yet #15 radiates light-blue streaks outward from the head, giving an open burst that contrasts with #14's contained olive backdrop.

lookingQuestion: How does the single flat olive background change the way you read the multicolored patches on the face compared to the patterned backgrounds in neighboring works?
ambiguities: The glasses lenses contain faint marks that may be reflections or text, but they are too small to read with certainty.
A signature-like mark appears in the lower-right corner but its exact lettering is unclear.
